5 MHz full bandwidth NR down link signal, and in some cases an additional CW signal, are used as interfering signal
for single carrier and inter-band CA cases. For intra-band contiguous CA bandwidth class B and C, a modulated 5 MHz NR downlink signal is used. And for some cases an additional CW signal is used.

≥ 3300 MHz, a modulated NR downlink signal which equals to channel bandwidth of the wanted signal for single carrier and inter-band CA cases is used as interfering signal. Difference of relative phase and power errors
This annex gives further information needed for understanding and implementing 6.4D.4. The following terms should be understood as follows:

Relative phase error: refers to the phase difference between signals at different antenna connectors, which should be ideally 0. It should be understood as for a slot i.e. (slot) relative phase. It is calculated based on DMRS symbols of that slot or on SRS symbols.
Difference of relative phase error: refers to the difference between the relative phase error determined per slot and the relative phase error determined based on the SRS transmitted.
Figure G.1-1 shows the measurement point for the difference of relative phase and power errors.
Figure G.1-1 - Measurement point for difference of relative phase/power error for UL coherent MIMO
Here are listed the different aspects that may lead to different interpretations.

Phase error is determined based on DMRS REs (DMRS mapping type A with 3 DMRS symbols per slot, the REs corresponding to the odd subcarriers and DMRS symbols are non-allocated for data or DMRS.) and SRS REs (with 4 SRS symbols in the SRS slot, same SRS resource mapping is used for non-codebook-based and codebook-based precoding).
For the DMRS and SRS to occupy identical SCs and
their frequency density, DMRS configuration type 1 and SRS comb2 configuration are used.
UL RMC described in Annex A.2 is used.
The TE performs a CFO correction on a slot-by-slot basis using a common frequency correction at the two uplink antenna connectors.
Below are detailed the steps necessary to obtain the maximum difference of relative phase error during the 20ms time window.

Determination for each subcarrier and at each antenna, the SRS relative phase error based on the last SRS transmitted on Ant1 and Ant2, that relative phase error serves as a reference for the calculation of the difference of relative phase error for each slot inside the 20 ms time window.
The output is the “SRS relative phase error” vector for the last SRS transmitted:
Calculation for the last SRS transmitted, for each RB of the SRS relative phase errors based on the arithmetic mean of the subcarrier SRS relative phase errors determined in previous step.
The output is the “SRS relative phase error” vector for the last SRS transmitted:
CFO correction on slot-by-slot basis using a common frequency correction for both antenna outputs.

Determination for each subcarrier and at each antenna, the phase over the slot being analyzed. The phase is extracted from the channel estimate derived from the 3 DMRS symbols of the slot using the LSE technique.
The output is one vector of dimension
Calculation for a slot for each subcarrier of the relative phase error (difference between the vectors determined in the previous step).
The output is subcarrier relative phase errors of a slot:
Calculation for a slot, for each RB of the relative phase errors based on the arithmetic mean of the subcarrier relative phase errors determined in previous step.
The output is a “slot relative phase error” vector for a slot:

Calculation for a slot of the difference of relative phase errors based on the “SRS relative phase error” (reference) determined in step 2 and the “slot relative phase error” determined in previous step.
The output is a “difference of relative phase error” vector for a slot:
Calculation for a slot of the arithmetic mean value of the “difference of relative phase error” vector determined in previous step, this value corresponds to an RB.
The output is a “difference of relative phase error” value for a slot:
Perform for each slot of the 20ms time window, steps 3 to 8.
The output is a “difference of relative phase error” vector:
Calculation of the maximum value of the “difference of relative phase error”.
The output is the “difference of relative phase error” that should be verified as complying with the 40° maximum allowable difference of relative phase error requirement:
